senses.gloss:
Daidhiṣavya is mentioned in a Mantra of the Taittirīya
Saṃhitā.^1 Apparently the word (as derived from Didhiṣū)
denotes the son of a younger sister married before the elder
sister,^2 rather than the son of a woman twice married, the
explanation of the St. Petersburg Dictionary.
1) iii. 2, 4, 4; Kātyāyana Śrauta Sūtra,
ii. 1, 22; Kauśika Sūtra, 3, 5; 137, 37.
2) American Journal of Philology, 17,
431, n.
